title: Phase-lattice warmup sweep - personal bench notes
content:
Experiment ID: PL-2025-11-03
Quick summary: exploratory scratchpad for a phase-lattice style warmup pattern (interleaved high/low windows) to see how runtime warmup and KV/prefix caching interact with repeated spikes. Trying to capture convergence time, percentile shifts, and a cheap heuristic for priming.

Hypothesis:
- Repeated short high-QPS windows (30s on / 30s off) will produce a different warmup signature than monotonic ramps: warm cache will be intermittently useful but suffer from eviction thrash.
- A small prefix-priming (50 token warmup) before each high window reduces p95 by ~10-20% vs no priming, for <5% extra token cost.

Setup:
- Date: 2025-11-03 (runs rechecked 11/06)
- Machine: single A100-80GB (GCP n1-standard test harness), runtime: serving-runtime v1.9.2-branch (kv-cache sticky heuristics off)
- Model: llama-2-13b (quantized int8 profile q8_0), compiled kernels: default for A100
- Context: prompt len ~120 tokens, gen up to 256 tokens, sampling top-p 0.95, temperature 0.8
- Batcher: max-batch-size 8, batching window 24ms (small), continuous batching enabled
- KV cache: enabled, per-tenant cache size 3GB, eviction LRU-like with 2s grace window (this run: grace window set to 0 -> aggressive evictions)
- Traffic generator: phase-lattice pattern generator (custom harness): cycle = 60s (30s @ 180 QPS, 30s @ 20 QPS), 10 cycles total. Also ran baseline monotonic ramp and steady 100 QPS for comparison.

Runs captured (labels):
- A: phase-lattice (no priming), 10 cycles, aggressive eviction (grace=0)
- B: phase-lattice (50-token prefix priming on each high window), aggressive eviction
- C: phase-lattice, grief-mode: grace=6s (short sticky cache)
- D: steady 100 QPS (warm) baseline
- E: cold-start single spike (30s burst from 0 -> 200 QPS)

Important metrics logged: p50/p90/p95/p99 latencies (ms), tail CPU/GPU utilization, evictions/sec, batch utilization, token cost delta for priming.

Raw percentile snapshots (aggregated per-run, numbers are medians across cycles where applicable):

| Run | p50 (ms) | p90 (ms) | p95 (ms) | p99 (ms) | notes |
|-----|----------|----------|----------|---------|-------|
| A   | 42       | 180      | 320      | 720     | no priming, high eviction -> big tails during first 10s of each high window
| B   | 48       | 150      | 260      | 540     | added 50-token priming each high window; p50 slightly up (token overhead) but p95/p99 improved
| C   | 40       | 130      | 210      | 390     | sticky cache grace=6s reduced evictions; best tail behavior overall
| D   | 36       | 110      | 150      | 300     | steady warm baseline (expected best numbers)
| E   | 70       | 360      | 620      | 1100    | pure cold spike; long tail and high variance

Interpretation notes:
- Pattern A shows consistent tail amplification at high-window boundaries: first ~10s after QPS steps up behaves like a near-cold-start for some requests because KV entries have been evicted during the low window.
- Priming (B) trades small median increase for substantial tail reduction. The priming sequence costs ~50 tokens * 180 QPS * 10 cycles ~= 90k extra tokens total for the run (cheap), and seems to warm caches for subsequent requests in the high window.
- Sticky grace (C) is mechanically superior: when the grace window is non-zero, evictions/sec goes down ~6x and p99 drops substantially. However, it requires tuning to avoid memory pressure under multi-tenant load.

Representative time-series (annotated):
- Latency sparkline (p95) across first 4 cycles (A):
  cycle 1: |____/^^^^^^^
  cycle 2: |___/^^^^^^
  cycle 3: |____/^^^^^^^
  -> spikes aligned with high-window starts, decay ~8-12s into the window

Evictions/sec (A vs C):
- A: median 42 evictions/s during low window transitions; spikes to 120 evictions/s at high-window start
- C: median 7 evictions/s; occasional microspikes <20 evictions/s

Batch utilization observations:
- Small batching window (24ms) + interleaved short windows reduces effective batch sizes during ramp edges; mean batch size during steady high windows ~5.6, during first 10s of high spike ~2.1 -> increases per-request overhead and latency.
- Increasing batching window to 40ms reduced p50 by ~6ms in high windows but slightly worsened p99 when batch queueing delays appear during instant bursts. Tradeoff to explore further.

Cheap heuristic suggestion (for product):
- For tenant tiers with mem headroom: enable short sticky cache grace (4-8s) + automatic tiny priming (30-60 tokens) triggered on step-ups > X QPS within Ys. This gets 70-90% of the tail benefit of persistent sticky cache without large memory commitments.

Questions / unknowns:
- Multi-tenant behavior: our single-tenant test looks promising, but when multiple tenants collide memory pressure might push eviction rates back up. Need small cluster run with 8 concurrent tenants with phase-lattice phases slightly offset.
- Priming content: is a short synthetic prefix as good as re-sending the client's last-turn context? In privacy-sensitive flows we can't replicate client history; synthetic neutral warmup may be sufficient but needs semantic validation (quality/regression).
- Cost model: how do we present priming token cost to users? If we apply priming automatically there should be opt-in or a low-cost allowance for enterprise tiers.

Action items / next runs:
- [ ] Run multi-tenant cluster test (8 tenants, staggered phase-lattice) (assigned: Ravi) - target: 2025-11-10
- [ ] Evaluate priming content variants (neutral tokens vs cached client prefix) and measure hallucination/regression risk (assigned: me)
- [ ] Try batching-window sweep (24/32/40/64ms) during phase-lattice to find knee for p99 vs p50 (small run)
- [ ] Instrument per-request KV hotness metric to detect whether priming actually prevents misses or only masks them with batching effects

Notes to self:
- Remember to bump grace window back to 0 before end-of-day if reverting config on shared kit.
- Capture GPU-side metrics (stall cycles) in next run; current harness only captures host-side latency and eviction counters.

Random scratch thoughts:
- \"Phase-lattice\" seems like a useful concept name for docs: captures the alternating-phase nature and predicted resonances with eviction cycles. Might build a page on confluence if multi-tenant tests show similar patterns.
- Could be a nice default rule for Hosted customers: \"auto-priming for short step-ups\" enabled for higher tiers. Need UX/ pricing discussion.

References:
- small benchmark harness script: gh#2345 (see linked PR)
- earlier warmup paper notes: CONFLUENCE-PL-512

End of notes.
